<thought>To meet the requirement of a single‑step synthesis from commercially available reagents, I identified a Suzuki‑Miyaura cross‑coupling that creates the C‑C double bond linking the phenyl ring to the alkene bearing the cyclobutane‑CF₃‑OH fragment. The reaction breaks an aryl‑halide bond and forms a C‑C double bond, which matches a standard Suzuki‑Miyaura template (template_id = 1023 in the database). Both precursors—phenylboronic acid (SMILES `B(c1ccccc1)`) and 3‑bromo‑1‑(trifluoromethyl)‑3‑hydroxy‑cyclobut‑1‑ene (SMILES `C= C(Br)C1CC[C@@]1(OH)C(F)(F)F`)—are commercially available and together cost well under $250. The retrosynthetic tree therefore consists of the target molecule, a single Suzuki‑Miyaura coupling step, and the two buyable precursors.
